# GitHub Copilot Workshops

I need your help creating 3 coding workshops that will help teach university student and recent post grad level of Developers expertise on how to effectively make the most of GitHub Copilot.

The languages for these 3 workshops should be constrainted to either Java or Python.
Each workshop should take about 10-15 minutes each to complete (with the assistance of GitHub Copilot)
Each exercise should provide detailed instructions on how to get started, but there should be at least one major detail left for the student to figure out on their own.

## Exercises

1. Unit test case generation

- Copilot can do a very good job of testing the obvious conditions, but how do we get better results for test case generation than just the obvious data test cases?
Clues: Non-obvious data types and tesgt conditions need to be spelt out clearly so GitHub Copilot can implement them.

1. Understand Code

- Complex code samples that can be explained using Copilot, but also refactored to be more human and AI coding assistant read-able.
Clues: highly complex code examples that use short variable names with no meaning, combine multi-line expressions onto a single line, no comments, etc

1. Code Conversion

- How do we know that a GitHub Copilot conversion from one language to another has provided an identical implementation?
Clues: Ensure that the existing codebase is well covered by test cases BEFORE converting to another language, this way to test cases are also converted and we can use this as a reassurnace that the code has equivilent functinality.


Each exercise should have clear instructions on how to get started, and what the expected end state should look like.

The project should have one concise README.md that acts as an entry point and directs the students to the correct starting point of each of the three workshop exercises.
